description: Mine the newly expanded landscape of robust neural-CA memories for motifs that naturally heal local perturbations and propagate domain walls. The hypothesis is that some of these healing rules correspond to reusable low-overhead forcing fronts after exact extraction.
mathematical_formalization: Sample a family of learned memory rules \{\phi_i\}. For each \phi_i, estimate robustness R_i under noise and damage, and define an extraction operator E(\phi_i) that maps stable wavefront motifs to candidate certificate modules. Search for high-R_i, low-S(E(\phi_i)) pairs on a Pareto frontier.
analogical_connections: A robust memory basin is treated as a reservoir of reusable proof fronts.
Error-correction boundaries in nonequilibrium memories become candidate elimination waves in relation space.
Noise resilience is a proxy for interface robustness under scale composition.
implementation_hypothesis: Use published memory-rule families as initialization for a local search restricted to small neighborhoods and discrete state alphabets. Extract small wavefront fragments from their dynamics and test whether those fragments compile into low-score modules more often than random CA rules do.
experiment_seed: Take a benchmark library of 100 learned memory rules and evaluate 3x3 or 5x5 local motifs cut from their trajectories. Track whether motif reuse improves score when inserted into the droplet compiler or graph-grammar pipeline.

closest_prior_art.title: Exploring the Landscape of Non-Equilibrium Memories with Neural Cellular Automata
A Toom rule that increases the thickness of sets
Universality for two-dimensional critical cellular automata

novelty_claim: The novelty is using memory-rule discovery as a motif mine for exact arithmetic witnesses, rather than claiming the Kakeya problem itself is a memory-phase question.
differentiation: This is not a reimplementation of nonequilibrium memories because the target observable is not lifetime or phase coexistence. It is the verifier score of extracted arithmetic certificates.
